answer: Each challenge commits to a future threshold-BLS beacon pulse whose unpredictable, publicly verifiable output is revealed only after submissions close. Because that pulse selects or transforms the task through a cryptographic derivation, a sybil swarm cannot precompute answers, hollow out participation through offline farming, or bias selection by spawning identities. Every participant must respond to the same later signal, while beacon quorum prevents any single operator from choosing it, and a prism-like audit trail exposes reuse.
